---
title: "After the day"
aliases:
  - /tracks/one-day-tools/after.html
---
A day on data tools ends with a report on your own machine, or a reproduction in your notes. The next steps are the ones that the day only demonstrated on the shared screen: putting the folder under version control, publishing the rendered report, and archiving a version of it. The workspace already carries the workflow that publishes the report once the folder is pushed to GitHub. The day also stops before the robustness exercise of the course, in which you would vary the analysis one decision at a time and send your results to a class chart. The [one-day course on methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does that on the same case, and the [exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) sets out Tasks 4 and 5 in full. The [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) takes each layer of the toolchain further, in modules that each stand on their own.

- [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) takes R further on the panel of the case, to the formats in which data arrive and the packages that fetch the data, the grammar of graphics, and the specification curve of the claim. The first steps, from objects to a first figure, are in the [module of the same name](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/intro-r.html) on the housing-audit site.
- [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) sets the three IDEs side by side.
- [Quarto and reproducible documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/quarto.html), on the housing-audit site, explains the document format of your report: the header, chunk options, figures, tables, cross-references and citations.
- [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html), on the AR4DS site, teaches version control from first principles and puts a repository of your own online.
- [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd) turns your own downloads from GESIS into the respondent file, the scales and the panel.
- [Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd) maps the archives, survey programmes and statistical offices, and follows the sources of this case step by step.
- [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) shows where finished work is deposited, what a licence allows others to do with it, and the preregistration templates.
- [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), from [The country-year level](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-aggregation) to [Within and between](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-re), sets out the statistics behind the three models that you reproduced.

The [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/) describes the four cases of the course and holds its setup and help pages. The [one-day course on open science](../eu-frames-one-day-open-science/index.qmd) takes the same case through reproduction, replication and preregistration, and the [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd) builds the data from the raw survey files.
